items.title: Morning Briefing: Oct. 26, 2026
items.excerpt: ISTANBUL (AA) - Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Monday, including Brazilian President Lula da Silva securing a historic fourth-term victory in a presidential runoff election, Serbia’s former President Aleksandar Vucic conceding that his electoral list had lost in snap parliamentary elections, US President Donald Trump reaffirming his strong support for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and Saudi Arabia reporting injuries and damage from debris after intercepting Houthi missiles. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva was declared the winner of a presidential runoff by the Superior Electoral Court (TSE), securing a fourth nonconsecutive term after defeating Flavio Bolsonaro in a closely contested race. With nearly all polling stations tallied, the TSE reported that Lula had secured 51.76% of valid votes against Bolsonaro's 48.24%, a margin of more than 4 million votes. Meanwhile, Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro announced that his legal team will formally petition to annul the country’s presidential runoff election following his narrow defeat to incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. In the initial vote on Oct. 4, Bolsonaro finished ahead with 47.03% of valid votes compared with Lula's 45.16%, setting the stage for three weeks of intense campaigning across Latin America's largest country. - Serbia’s Vucic concedes election defeat as student-backed opposition leads parliamentary vote Serbia’s former President Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in snap parliamentary elections as preliminary projections showed a student-backed opposition list winning the most seats. Speaking at the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in Belgrade, Vucic conceded that his electoral list had lost, according to preliminary projections.
